mcqs.q: Implanted radioactive sources are used in radiotherapy to:
options: Image an organ from outside the body
Expose cancerous tissue to radiation from inside or close to the tumour
Record a worker's accumulated dose
Slow down neutrons in a reactor core
mcqs.why: Besides aimed gamma rays from cobalt-60, implanted radioactive sources expose cancerous tissue in radiotherapy, per the notes.

lessons.title: Basic Forces of Nature
lessons.notes_html:
Four Basic Forces

There are four fundamental forces of nature. On the scale of elementary particles the gravitational force has negligible effect.

ForceActs betweenRelative strengthRole
Strong nuclearQuarks, nucleons1Holds nucleons together, range about 10-15 m
ElectromagneticElectric charges10-2Chemistry and light
Weak nuclearParticles in beta decay10-13Responsible for beta decay
GravitationalAll masses10-39Always attractive, governs large-scale universe

The strong force is the strongest but acts only over about 10-15 m. The weak force acts over even shorter distances. The electromagnetic force acts between charges, and gravity acts between masses and is always attractive.

mcqs.q: How many fundamental forces of nature are listed in the notes?
options: Two: gravitational and electromagnetic only
Four: strong nuclear, electromagnetic, weak nuclear and gravitational
Three: strong, weak and gravitational only
Five, including a separate frictional force
mcqs.why: There are four fundamental forces: strong nuclear, electromagnetic, weak nuclear and gravitational, as listed in the notes.

mcqs.q: The strong nuclear force has relative strength 1 and acts between:
options: Electric charges only, over unlimited range
All masses, governing the large-scale universe
Quarks and nucleons, holding nucleons together over about 10^-15 m
Particles in beta decay only
mcqs.why: The strong force, relative strength 1, acts between quarks and nucleons and holds nucleons together, with range about 10^-15 m.

mcqs.q: The electromagnetic force has relative strength:
options: 1, acting between nucleons only
10^-13, responsible for beta decay
10^-39, acting between all masses
10^-2, acting between electric charges and responsible for chemistry and light
mcqs.why: The table gives the electromagnetic force relative strength 10^-2, acting between electric charges, with role in chemistry and light.

mcqs.q: The weak nuclear force, with relative strength 10^-13, is responsible for:
options: Beta decay
Holding nucleons together
Chemistry and light
Governing the large-scale universe
mcqs.why: The weak nuclear force acts between particles in beta decay with relative strength 10^-13, as shown in the forces table.

mcqs.q: The gravitational force has relative strength 10^-39 and is:
options: Sometimes repulsive, acting between charges only
Always attractive, acting between all masses and governing the large-scale universe
The strongest force, acting over 10^-15 m only
Responsible for beta decay in nuclei
mcqs.why: Gravity acts between all masses with relative strength 10^-39, is always attractive and governs the large-scale universe.

mcqs.q: The strong force is the strongest force but acts only over about:
options: Unlimited distance with no limit
mcqs.why: The notes state the strong force is the strongest but acts only over about 10^-15 m, the size scale of the nucleus.

mcqs.q: On the scale of elementary particles, which force has negligible effect?
options: The strong nuclear force
The electromagnetic force
The weak nuclear force
The gravitational force
mcqs.why: On the scale of elementary particles the gravitational force has negligible effect, because its relative strength is only 10^-39.

mcqs.q: Put the four forces in order of decreasing relative strength.
options: Strong (1), electromagnetic (10^-2), weak (10^-13), gravitational (10^-39)
Gravitational (1), weak (10^-2), electromagnetic (10^-13), strong (10^-39)
Electromagnetic (1), strong (10^-2), gravitational (10^-13), weak (10^-39)
Strong (1), weak (10^-2), electromagnetic (10^-13), gravitational (10^-39)
mcqs.why: Relative strengths from the table: strong 1, electromagnetic 10^-2, weak 10^-13 and gravitational 10^-39, in that decreasing order.

mcqs.q: The weak force acts over distances that are:
options: Much longer than the electromagnetic range
Even shorter than the strong force's range
The same as the gravitational range
About the size of an atom, 10^-10 m
mcqs.why: The notes state the weak force acts over even shorter distances than the strong force, whose range is about 10^-15 m.

mcqs.q: Which force acts between electric charges?
options: The strong nuclear force
The weak nuclear force
The electromagnetic force
The gravitational force
mcqs.why: The electromagnetic force acts between charges, while the strong force acts between quarks and nucleons and gravity between masses.

lessons.title: Elementary Particles and Their Classification
lessons.notes_html:
Elementary and Subatomic Particles

Subatomic particles are all particles smaller than an atom, including protons, neutrons and electrons. Elementary particles are truly fundamental, with no internal structure: the quarks and the leptons. Protons and neutrons are subatomic but not elementary, because they are made of quarks; the electron is both subatomic and elementary.

Fermions and Bosons

FermionsBosons
SpinHalf-integral: 1/2, 3/2, ...Integral: 0, 1, ...
RuleObey Pauli exclusion principleNo exclusion, many can share one state
RoleBuilding blocks of matterCarry forces
ExamplesQuarks, leptons, electronPhoton, mesons, Higgs boson

The six quarks are up, down, charm, strange, top and bottom. The six leptons are the electron, muon, tau and their three neutrinos. Bosons that carry forces are the photon (electromagnetic), W and Z bosons (weak), gluons (strong) and the Higgs boson, which gives other particles mass. Particles with half-integral spin are fermions; baryons have the highest mass among photons, leptons, mesons and baryons.

Hadrons

Hadrons are composite particles made of quarks. Baryons are made of three quarks, such as protons and neutrons, and have the highest masses. Mesons are made of a quark and an antiquark, such as pions and kaons. Well over a hundred hadrons are known, including lambda, sigma, xi and omega baryons.

Key Points

  • A nucleus has Z protons and A - Z neutrons; it is written as AZX, and 1 u = 931 MeV.
  • Isotopes share Z, isobars share A, isotones share neutron number, isomers share Z and A but differ in energy state.
  • A mass spectrograph separates isotopes by mass-to-charge ratio in a magnetic field.
  • Binding energy is Δm c2; binding energy per nucleon peaks near iron-56, explaining both fission and fusion.
  • Radioactivity is spontaneous and unaffected by temperature or pressure; alpha is most ionizing, gamma most penetrating.
  • Decay follows N = N0 e-λ t with T1/2 = 0.693 / λ and 1 Ci = 3.7 x 1010 Bq.
  • Fission of uranium-235 gives about 200 MeV and 2.5 neutrons; a reactor uses fuel, moderator, control rods, coolant and shielding.
  • Fusion joins light nuclei, powers the Sun by the proton-proton chain, and gives more energy per nucleon than fission.
  • Exposure is measured in roentgen, absorbed dose in rad or gray, dose equivalent in rem or sievert; tracers and radiotherapy use radiation in medicine.
  • Four forces: strong 1, electromagnetic 10-2, weak 10-13, gravitational 10-39; fermions build matter, bosons carry forces.

mcqs.q: Subatomic particles are all particles smaller than an atom, while elementary particles are:
options: Made of three quarks each
Only the protons and neutrons
Truly fundamental, with no internal structure: the quarks and the leptons
Particles that carry forces only
mcqs.why: Elementary particles are truly fundamental with no internal structure: the quarks and the leptons, as defined in the notes.

mcqs.q: Protons and neutrons are subatomic but not elementary because they are:
options: Larger than an atom
Without any mass
Made of photons
Made of quarks
mcqs.why: Protons and neutrons are subatomic but not elementary because they are made of quarks; the electron is both subatomic and elementary.

mcqs.q: Fermions have spin that is:
options: Half-integral: 1/2, 3/2, ... and they obey the Pauli exclusion principle
Integral: 0, 1, ... and many can share one state
Always zero, and they carry forces
Half-integral, and they never obey any exclusion rule
mcqs.why: Fermions have half-integral spin and obey the Pauli exclusion principle; they are the building blocks of matter.

mcqs.q: Bosons have integral spin, carry forces, and:
options: Obey the Pauli exclusion principle strictly
Have no exclusion rule, so many can share one state
Are the building blocks of matter only
Always have half-integral spin
mcqs.why: Bosons have integral spin 0, 1, ..., no exclusion applies so many can share one state, and they carry forces.

mcqs.q: The six quarks named in the notes are:
options: Electron, muon, tau and their three neutrinos
Proton, neutron, pion, kaon, lambda and sigma
Up, down, charm, strange, top and bottom
Photon, gluon, W, Z, Higgs and meson
mcqs.why: The six quarks are up, down, charm, strange, top and bottom; the electron, muon, tau and neutrinos are the leptons.

mcqs.q: The six leptons are:
options: Up, down, charm, strange, top and bottom
The photon, W and Z bosons and gluons
Protons, neutrons and electrons
The electron, muon, tau and their three neutrinos
mcqs.why: The six leptons are the electron, muon, tau and their three neutrinos, as listed in the notes.

mcqs.q: The Higgs boson is important because it:
options: Gives other particles mass
Carries the strong force between nucleons
Is the carrier of the electromagnetic force
Makes up protons and neutrons as a quark
mcqs.why: Force-carrying bosons include the photon, W and Z, and gluons, and the Higgs boson, which gives other particles mass.

mcqs.q: Hadrons are composite particles made of quarks; baryons such as protons and neutrons are made of:
options: A quark and an antiquark
Three quarks
Two quarks only
Six leptons
mcqs.why: Baryons are made of three quarks, such as protons and neutrons, while mesons are made of a quark and an antiquark.

mcqs.q: Mesons, such as pions and kaons, are made of:
options: Three quarks
Three antiquarks only
A quark and an antiquark
A lepton and a quark
mcqs.why: Mesons are hadrons made of a quark and an antiquark, such as pions and kaons, as stated in the notes.

mcqs.q: Among photons, leptons, mesons and baryons, which have the highest mass?
options: Photons
Leptons
Mesons
Baryons
mcqs.why: The notes state baryons have the highest mass among photons, leptons, mesons and baryons, and over a hundred hadrons are known.
